segments.title: Opening: date and location of the follow-up interview
segments.summary: Allen tests the recorder; Steinau gives the date, 28 May 1983, and his home in Las Cruces, New Mexico.

segments.title: Where Steinau heard Sharkey, Raymond Burke and Johnny Wiggs
segments.summary: Steinau recalls hearing Sharkey at the Famous Door and Parisian Room concerts, Burke only with Wiggs, and Wiggs at a jazz club meeting and the record shop back room.

segments.title: Ralston Crawford, photography advice and walking in parades
segments.summary: Crawford advised looking at many paintings and photographs; the two discuss whether white spectators walked in time to parade music.

segments.title: George Lewis band at El Morocco and trumpeters Talbert and Kid Howard
segments.summary: Steinau recalls the El Morocco engagement from about early 1950 and the trumpet changes after Elmer Talbert's illness, with Allen on the Kid Howard period and the air-conditioned stage.

segments.title: New Orleans Jazz Club officers and members
segments.summary: Myra Menville as secretary and Dr. Sushan as active member; neither man remembers jazz club people at Manny's or El Morocco.

segments.title: Joan Whitehead, flexichrome and her photographs
segments.summary: Steinau explains Joan Whitehead's Kodak work and the flexichrome coloring process; he has one of her Johnny Wiggs prints.

segments.title: Ted Lewis at the Blue Room and Roosevelt Hotel
segments.summary: Steinau saw Ted Lewis as a teenager, vaudeville-like; Allen recalls Sharkey working the Blue Room then the Famous Door.

segments.title: Summer park jazz concerts and Steinau's externships
segments.summary: Neither remembers much of the summer park bands; Steinau was away three early-1950s summers and did externships.

segments.chapter: Parisian Room and Bourbon Street clubs
segments.title: Externships at Pineville and Mercy Hospital
segments.summary: Steinau describes his medical externships doing histories and physicals, housed in a condemned building.

segments.chapter: Parisian Room and Bourbon Street clubs
segments.title: Junior Dixielanders and Sunday afternoons at the Parisian Room
segments.summary: Steinau went rarely to the Parisian Room Sunday concerts with Tony Almerico and heard several outfits.

segments.chapter: Parisian Room and Bourbon Street clubs
segments.title: Fazola, Federico, Butera and other Parisian Room players
segments.summary: Steinau names players he heard at the Parisian Room, including Fazola, Frank Federico and Sam DeKemel, and dates his visits to 1947-48.

segments.chapter: Parisian Room and Bourbon Street clubs
segments.title: Comparing Manny's and El Morocco
segments.summary: El Morocco was a small typical Bourbon Street club; Manny's was larger, informal with dancing, and the band played a wider repertoire there.

segments.chapter: Parisian Room and Bourbon Street clubs
segments.title: Bawdy tunes and Joe Watkins's dedication at Manny's
segments.summary: Repertoire of mildly suggestive songs at Manny's and Allen's memory of Watkins dedicating a blues.

segments.chapter: Parisian Room and Bourbon Street clubs
segments.title: Mirrored ball, bandstand layout and Ken Collier photo
segments.summary: The two recall the mirrored ball, bandstand position and redecoration at Manny's, and Steinau's lack of contact with Ken Collier.

segments.chapter: Parisian Room and Bourbon Street clubs
segments.title: Whether bands used a tip kitty
segments.summary: Neither saw a kitty on Bourbon Street; tips were handed to the band directly.

segments.chapter: Parisian Room and Bourbon Street clubs
segments.title: Dating the June 1950 Lewis session and timing the tunes
segments.summary: Allen found the George Lewis Good Time Jazz session dated 5 June 1950; they marvel at how consistently the tunes timed out.

segments.chapter: Parisian Room and Bourbon Street clubs
segments.title: Mardi Gras 1950, Ciro's, dates and dancing
segments.summary: Recollections of Mardi Gras 1950, who had dates, and their reluctance to dance.

segments.chapter: Kubrick, Look and the Lewis band
segments.title: Sound trucks and bands on advertising trucks
segments.summary: Steinau saw more sound trucks than band trucks, and they discuss the difficulty of photographing them.

segments.chapter: Kubrick, Look and the Lewis band
segments.title: Kubrick and Roddy of Look and the effect of the article on Lewis
segments.summary: Steinau praises Kubrick's photography and says the 1950 Look article revived George Lewis's career, bringing travel and records.

segments.chapter: Kubrick, Look and the Lewis band
segments.title: Lutton's and a night out on Bourbon Street
segments.summary: Steinau visited Lutton's a few times; one long night took in Lutton's, Happy Landing and Mama Lou's.

segments.chapter: Kubrick, Look and the Lewis band
segments.title: Otto's party recordings and the Herb Moran session photos
segments.summary: Questions about Lewis and Herb Moran prints and Otto's and Greenwood's taping; Steinau photographed the Moran session with unsatisfying results.

segments.title: Ace Watson and the grand marshal tradition
segments.summary: Ace Watson as grand marshal at funerals, the reversible sash, Allen's umbrella and how grand marshals behaved.

segments.title: Who hired bands for private parties
segments.summary: Private parties and committees hired bands; the friends' own parties at Otto's treated the band as social guests.

segments.chapter: Auditions, musicians and the jazz club
segments.title: Band auditions and rehearsals
segments.summary: Steinau attended auditions more than rehearsals, including Billie and De De Pierce, a Lutton's group and Emile Barnes in the record shop.

segments.chapter: Auditions, musicians and the jazz club
segments.title: Musicians and drinking
segments.summary: They recall how much the musicians drank, Jim Robinson's bottle, and the sweating of playing.

segments.chapter: Auditions, musicians and the jazz club
segments.title: Jazz Club job-finding, the Sushans and leftover note items
segments.summary: The Jazz Club found work for favorites; Edmond Sushan donated records; Allen runs through items they already covered.

segments.chapter: Auditions, musicians and the jazz club
segments.title: Jazz Club meetings, Black performers and Mono Lee
segments.summary: Questions about Monday meetings and Black performers at the club, and when a woman associate of Greenwood arrived.

segments.title: Musicians' day jobs
segments.summary: Talbert, Joe Watkins and others held daytime jobs such as janitor; George Lewis was a longshoreman.

segments.title: Mixing socially with the musicians and the Harmony Inn
segments.summary: They never ate with the musicians but visited homes and parties, nervously, and recall a large club where Emile Barnes played.

segments.title: Tape check and the decor of old clubs
segments.summary: After a recorder check, Steinau recalls the old-fashioned decor of the clubs and neighbours' remarks about parties.

segments.title: Greenwood's journal, late 1949: Manny's, Bergen, Campbell's
segments.summary: Allen reads journal dates for Manny's, Stuart Bergen at a fraternity party and a Campbell's visit; Steinau recalls his roommate who told him of the record shop.

segments.title: Greenwood journal: taping the Lewis band and Lewis's age
segments.summary: Debate over who taped Lewis at Bourbon Street, Lawrence Marrero's heart and George Lewis's plan to quit; then Feb 1950 outings with Look staff.

segments.title: Eating while listening to jazz
segments.summary: They find that clubs in the era hardly served food, Lutton's being a beer hall, with a later Sunday afternoon store venue.

segments.title: More journal entries and visits to a house
segments.summary: Journal items on the funeral, Roger Wolfe interview, a Storyville house on Esplanade and a place they visited.

segments.title: Herb Moran at the Rainbow Bar and the Lewis band at El Morocco
segments.summary: Journal entries from May 1950 on Moran's group, the record shop band and the Lewis El Morocco opening.

segments.title: Gagliano anniversary party, pinball and the WTPS radio show
segments.summary: They went to an anniversary party with the Lewis band, then rode to the WTPS radio program.

segments.chapter: Noon Johnson and other local figures
segments.title: Noon Johnson, the bazooka and Lafitte's Guesthouse
segments.summary: Steinau describes Noon Johnson playing his homemade bazooka with McNeil Brown at a bar, and they pin down the location.

segments.chapter: Noon Johnson and other local figures
segments.title: Noon Johnson's singing, Kid Clayton and local color
segments.summary: Allen recalls Noon and Kid Clayton at Lafitte's, Noon's recordings with Bunk, and his singing at restaurants.

segments.chapter: Noon Johnson and other local figures
segments.title: Outside wives and musicians as ladies' men
segments.summary: Reminiscence about Lawrence Marrero's family and the custom of a married wife and an outside wife.

segments.chapter: Noon Johnson and other local figures
segments.title: Greenwood's going-away party
segments.summary: They cannot place some names in Greenwood's note of his going-away party before Michigan library school.

segments.title: Dutchess Tavern, Richard Batiste and what counts as tradition
segments.summary: Allen recalls Frank Murray's band at the Dutchess, Batiste's trumpet trill resembling Bunk, and how traditions start.

segments.title: The musicians' union and non-union bands
segments.summary: Whether Emile Barnes and Bourbon Street bands were union, and Steinau's visits to Manny's.

segments.title: Travelling to Manny's by streetcar and bus
segments.summary: The long multi-transfer trip across town to hear Lewis, with late service and fares.

segments.title: Cheap beer, GI Bill money and buying records
segments.summary: Beer prices, living on GI Bill money and the cost of buying records, which were their main entertainment.

segments.title: Ricard Alexis's business card and Celestin's Paddock band
segments.summary: A business card leads to Celestin's band at the Paddock Lounge, personnel, clowning and slapsticks.
